{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=March 2021}} {{Infobox NCAA team season | mode = Basketball | year = 2021–22 | team = Nebraska Cornhuskers | image = Nebraska Cornhuskers logo.svg | image_size = | conference = Big Ten Conference | short_conf = Big Ten | record = 10–22 | conf_record = 4–16 | head_coach = [[Fred Hoiberg]] | hc_year = 3rd | asst_coach1 = Matt Abdelmassih | asst_coach2 = Armon Gates | asst_coach3 = Nate Loenser | asst_coach4 = [[Doc Sadler]] | CoachRank = | APRank = | stadium = [[Pinnacle Bank Arena]] | champion = | bowl = | bowl_result = }} {{2021–22 Big Ten Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2021–22 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]] in the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Cornhuskers were led by third-year head coach [[Fred Hoiberg]] and played their home games at [[Pinnacle Bank Arena]] in [[Lincoln, Nebraska]] as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. They finished the season 10–22, 4–16 in [[2021–22 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a tie for last place. As the No. 13 seed in the [[2022 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they lost to [[2021–22 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|Northwestern]] in the first round. ==Previous season== In a season limited due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], the [[2020–21 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Cornhuskers]] finished the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 7–20, 3–16 in [[2020–21 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish last place. As the No. 14 seed in the [[2021 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], the Cornhuskers lost to No. 11-seeded [[2020–21 Penn State Nittany Lions basketball team|Penn State]].{{Cite web|last= NU Athletic Communications|title=Huskers Fall in Final Seconds|url= https://huskers.com/news/2019/11/29/huskers-fall-in-final-seconds |access-date=2021-03-22|website=Huskers.com|language=en-US}} ==Offseason== ===Departures=== Due to COVID-19, the NCAA ruled that the 2020–21 season would not count against the eligibility of any competitor in any of the organization's winter sports, including basketball. This in turn meant that all players active in the 2020–21 season, regardless of their academic classification, could return in 2021–22. This also led the NBA and its players union to agree that graduating seniors, who are normally automatically eligible for the NBA draft, had to declare their eligibility for the 2021 draft. {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
